title: Generic closedness rigidity for an existing torus homomorphism
statement: Let $S$ be a normal integral locally Noetherian scheme with generic point $\eta$. Let $P\to S$ be a torus, meaning a smooth affine commutative group scheme of finite presentation which is fppf locally isomorphic to $\mathbf G_m^r$ for a finite $r\geq0$. Let $G\to S$ be smooth, separated, commutative and of finite presentation, with semiabelian geometric fibres. If an $S$-group homomorphism $f:P\to G$ is already given and $f_\eta:P_\eta\to G_\eta$ is a closed immersion, then $f$ is a closed immersion. The scheme, normality, finite-presentation, group, fibre, torus and topology conventions are [def-pc-scheme] [def-pc-integral-scheme] [pqf-def-locnoeth] [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] [def-sc-group-scheme] [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] [def-sfb-semiabelian-geometric-fibres] [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] [def-pc-base-change] [def-sc-gm-ga] [def-sfb-tori-multiplicative-type] [def-weil-closed-immersion] [def-pc-fppf-site].

proof.text: Fix $s\in S$ and put $R=\mathcal O_{S,s}$, $F=\kappa(\eta)$. The ring $R$ is a Noetherian local domain: choose a Noetherian affine neighbourhood and use [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]. Use [lem-trf-fppf-covering-base-change] to pull back an fppf splitting cover of $P$ to $\operatorname{Spec}R$ and choose a point over its closed point. Let $B$ be the local ring there and $k$ its residue field. By [def-pc-fppf-site] and [def-weil-flat-morphism], $B$ is a nonzero flat local $R$-algebra and $P_B$ is split. Choose the cover chart affine of finite presentation; [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] and [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] make $B$ Noetherian. Apply [lem-sfb-split-local-special-kernel-lifting] to $f_B$. It gives $M=\mathbf Z^r/L$ and a closed subgroup $H=D_B(M)\subset P_B$ killed by $f_B$, with $H_k=\ker(f_k)$.

proof.text: Form $K=P\times_{G,e_G}S$. The unit $e_G$ is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-section-separated-closed-immersion], since $G\to S$ is separated. Its base change makes $K\hookrightarrow P$ closed [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. Since $P$ is affine over $S$, the affine description in [def-weil-closed-immersion] writes $K$ over any Noetherian affine base $\operatorname{Spec}A$ as $\operatorname{Spec}E$ for a finite-type $A$-algebra $E$. The ring $E$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Let $J=\ker(E\xrightarrow{e_K^*}A)$. The structure map splits this augmentation, so $E=A\oplus J$ as $A$-modules. Step 2 gives $J\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)=0$ for every prime $\mathfrak p$ of $A$. For a prime $\mathfrak q$ of $E$ lying over $\mathfrak p$, this implies $J_{\mathfrak q}=\mathfrak pE_{\mathfrak q}J_{\mathfrak q}$. This ideal is finitely generated because $E$ is Noetherian, and $\mathfrak pE_{\mathfrak q}$ is contained in the maximal ideal of $E_{\mathfrak q}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-jacobson] to get $J_{\mathfrak q}=0$. An element nonzero in $J$ has proper annihilator contained in some maximal ideal, where its localization remains nonzero. Hence $J=0$ and $K\simeq S$.

proof.text: For any $S$-scheme $T$ and $x,y\in P(T)$ with $f(x)=f(y)$, the element $xy^{-1}$ belongs to $K(T)=\{1\}$, so $x=y$. Thus $f$ is a monomorphism on every test scheme, including nonreduced ones. Apply [lem-sfb-relative-torus-monomorphism-closed] to $P$, $G$ and this already given $f$; $P$ is a torus and $G$ is separated of finite presentation by hypothesis. It follows that $f$ is a closed immersion.

The item statement and stmt_deps are byte-equal to live, and live still has the item unsplit. Proof: step 1 pulls the fppf splitting cover back to O_{S,s} (fppf-covering-base-change), takes the flat Noetherian local ring B there and applies the new lifting node. Step 2 uses flatness (B is R-torsion-free, so B⊗F≠0), the generic closed immersion (so H_C=1) and the group-algebra basis to get M=0; the special kernel and the κ(s)-kernel are then trivial (field-extension-tensor-injective). Step 3: e_G is closed, K=Spec E, E=A⊕J, J_q=pE_qJ_q, and Nakayama gives J=0. Step 4: monic on all T, then the new monic-torus node. All checked against the cited statements. New node lem-sfb-split-local-special-kernel-lifting is true: I checked it myself (field subgroups of D_k(Z^r) are D_k(Z^r/L); a hom trivial modulo a square-zero ideal is trivial for any target group, by comparing degree-m parts; coefficientwise Krull intersection). Tested on [n] with μ_p kernel, the constant map, r=0 and nonreduced R. New node lem-sfb-relative-torus-monomorphism-closed is Conrad, Reductive group schemes, Thm 5.3.5 specialized to tori, over any S with a separated finitely presented target. The Conrad PDF is not in literature/, so I judged it from my knowledge of the theorem. Neither new node restates the item or duplicates an existing node: the existing monic⇒closed and subgroup-classification nodes are field-level, and rg found no relative node.
